sections.section: The running case and a dated debt state
sections.teaching_construction: Original loan 120000 dollars, six years, 6% effective annual loan rate; dated before/after balances, positive borrower-payment convention, A installment distinct from A(t) amount function; restated annuity factors with empty-sum and zero-rate cases, indexing and time units.

sections.section: Amortization starts with interest on the preceding balance
sections.lecture_material: Interest on preceding balance, interest-first payment decomposition, amortization; lecture 1000-rupee 10% example with payments 200, 500 and 539.
sections.teaching_construction: Recurrence derived from before/after timing; original Figure 10.1; positive/zero/negative principal repayment boundary, principal and interest total checks.

sections.section: Choosing the level installment and building the schedule
sections.lecture_material: Level installment L/a-angle-n, three-year 1000-rupee schedule and six-year 5000 example.
sections.teaching_construction: Equation of value derivation, positive-amortization proof, exact running schedule Table 10.1 with totals and display-rounding distinction, early principal repayment mechanism; duplicate six-year lecture values discussed in implementation.

sections.section: Prospective and retrospective balances are the same dated value
sections.lecture_material: Prospective B_m=A*a-angle-(n-m), retrospective L*(1+i)^m-A*s-angle-m; equality by substitution.
sections.teaching_construction: Full cancellation proof and independent recurrence induction; original before-payment formula, general unequal-payment cash-flow split, terminal residual and missed-payment completeness conditions, same-rate restriction, endpoints and running B3 check.

sections.section: Why principal portions grow while interest portions fall
sections.lecture_material: Normalized principal a-angle-n with installment 1; interest 1-v^(n-t+1), principal v^(n-t+1), outstanding a-angle-(n-t), decreasing interest and increasing principal.
sections.teaching_construction: Scaling by A, geometric principal ratio, total-principal proof, total-interest identity, numerical running-case check and the exact threshold for interest to exceed principal; zero-rate and one-payment boundaries.

sections.section: A spreadsheet, a calculator and a monetary ledger
sections.lecture_material: Spreadsheet schedule with fixed rate/installment cells and preceding-row balance; monthly car-loan example with 1000000 rupees, 60 installments and annual 8% divided by 12; 5000 six-year table.
sections.research_extension: TI guidebook pp21-22: I/Y nominal, P/Y and C/Y, END/BGN, inflow/outflow signs, BAL after selected payment and rounded PMT in amortization calculations.
sections.teaching_construction: Exact-model versus cent-ledger distinction; original half-up cent ledger and final payment 24403.49; two 8% conventions; L55 correction of misplaced decimal distinguished from recalculated full-precision value.

sections.section: Irregular payments require a cash-flow equation
sections.lecture_material: Four-month 100000-rupee loan at nominal 8% with payments X,X,2X,2X; lab truncation of monthly rate to 0.0066; preceding 500000 five-year 7% example.
sections.teaching_construction: Full discounted equation and shifted two-payment block; exact 1/150 rate gives X16982.98 and Table 10.2, exact zero terminal balance; prospective intermediate check and zero-rate limit; discrepancy of rounded-factor lecture values explained.

sections.section: A rate reset changes the future schedule from today's balance
sections.lecture_material: 4000000-rupee twenty-year loan, nominal monthly 5% rising to 5.5% after payment24; revised installment or unchanged installment with extended term; early rate/factor truncations.
sections.teaching_construction: Exact old rate balance by both methods, new remaining-216-period equation, monotonic-payment argument, logarithmic remaining-term derivation with interest-only boundary, whole-month drop amount and explicit dates; no forced-zero residual.

sections.section: A sinking fund builds an asset while the principal remains due
sections.lecture_material: Interest-only lender payments plus sinking fund deposits, original loan normalized to a-angle-n; equal-rate interest1-v^n plus depositv^n; 5000-dollar fund table.
sections.teaching_construction: Separate principal and fund ledgers; j defined as effective fund rate per same loan-payment period with local scope and frequency conversion; fund recurrence, deposit derivation, original Table 10.3, zero-return case and no double counting of maturity transfer.

sections.section: Equal rates give equal outflows and a net-debt identity
sections.lecture_material: Different loan and fund rates, total outflow L*(i+1/s-angle-n at j).
sections.teaching_construction: Equal-rate cash-outflow algebra, original net-debt recurrence proof, loan interest less fund interest cost identity, unequal-rate difference, monotonicity proof with n=1 exception and zero-rate checks, deterministic versus expected return boundary.

Table 10.4 compares amortization with annual fund rates6% and3%; gross principal, fund and net positions at year3, totals, explanation that larger deposits can give a larger intermediate fund at a lower return; answers opening decision with model scope.

sections.section: Executable checks of the debt and fund ledgers
sections.teaching_construction: Standard-library program: exact fraction direct sums versus factors, recurrence/prospective/retrospective/net fund at seven dates, principal sums and ratios, zero/one-payment checks, exact irregular terminal balance and reset balance; Decimal cent ledger; float monthly conversion/log term/bisection; four ValueError cases; tested sign and unequal-rate mutations.

sections.section: What the model captures and what changes the calculation
sections.research_extension: SOA October2026 syllabus p3: Loans15-25%, balance, interest/principal, final-payment and refinancing objectives.
sections.teaching_construction: Captures/misses audit: variable contractual rates as period products, fees as dated flows, default and uncertain fund returns, tax/cost/access effects and inflation; no claims about actual contract law or current borrowing offers.

sections.lecture_material: Lab inspired the reset problem; lecture formulas supply the concepts. All six questions use original constructions or original numerical inputs.
sections.teaching_construction: Six complete solutions: derive prepayment and interest saving; exam-style seventh-payment interest and dated balances; nominal/effective monthly convention; missed-payment counterexample and arrears balloon; rate-reset design with whole-month drop; budget judgment and unique inverse fund-rate root.
